research_question: Are self-interpretable graph neural network explanations faithful, stable, and predictively useful under graph distribution shift?

gold_papers.title: Graph Information Bottleneck
gold_papers.rationale: Foundational IB objective for graph rationale — GSAT/PGIB/VGIB in the workspace build on it. An external gate must surface it so the system does not claim the IB-rationale combination is novel.

gold_papers.title: Invariant Risk Minimization
gold_papers.rationale: Foundational invariant-feature learning under environment shift. DIR in the workspace derives from it; overlaps the 'invariant + distribution shift' axis of the research question.

gold_papers.title: Graph Rationalization with Environment-based Augmentations
gold_papers.rationale: Explicitly combines graph rationalization (invariant rationales) with environment-based augmentation for OOD — a close prior that challenges the novelty of 'invariant rationale under graph shift'.

gold_papers.title: Interpretation of Neural Networks is Fragile
gold_papers.rationale: Shows explanations are unstable under small adversarial perturbations of the input — direct counter-evidence against assuming explanations stay stable, relevant to the 'stability' axis.

gold_papers.title: Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
gold_papers.rationale: Cautions that saliency-style explanations can be insensitive to model and data randomization — qualifies any claim that explanation faithfulness is measurable without rigorous baselines.

gold_papers.title: Reliable Post hoc Explanations: Modeling Uncertainty in Explainability
gold_papers.rationale: Explanations should carry uncertainty — qualifies the predictive-utility and reliability axes of the research question.

gold_papers.title: Explainability Methods for Graph Convolutional Neural Networks
gold_papers.rationale: Early systematic evaluation of GNN explanation methods — overlaps the evaluation-protocol axis and should be recalled as related work.
